To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

jugular bulb oximeter data obtained during the first 12 hours after traumatic brain injury reveal an incidence of 38% of abnormal cerebral oxygen utilization, with a predominance (80%) of jugular bulb saturation below the normal range.

1. jugular bulb oximeter measurements in the early hours following severe traumatic brain injury are often abnormal (in 38% of patients), with desaturation being the most common finding; 2. the incidence of abnormal jugular oximetry values is higher than the incidence of abnormal cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) values; 3. the incidence of low jugular bulb oxygen saturations is higher than the combined incidence of low CPP values and high arterial carbon dioxide tensions;

jugular bulb desaturations are common in the first 12 hours after severe traumatic brain insult, that these desaturations are related to systemic factors (e.g. lowered cerebral perfusion and/or lowered arterial carbon dioxide), and that these desaturatations are associated with an increased risk of poor outcome.

the analysis of very early jugualr bulb oximetry after head injury.
the early monitoring of the severely head-injured patient and its implications for the emergency medical management.

early jugular bulb desaturations are related to a lowered cerebral perfusions pressure and a low arterial carbon dioxide tension.
the initial jugular bulb saturation value is a good indicator of the cerebral oxygenation status, but it is not an absolute indicator of outcome.
the initial jugular bulb saturation value is a useful parameter to detect and to quantify inadequate cerebral perfusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early use of jugular bulb oxymetry is a useful and reliable tool for the early detection of inadequate cerebral oxygenation.
the early jugular bulb desaturations observed in this study were related to systemic factors that could be corrected by appropriate therapy.
in patients with severe brain injury, the initial jugular bulb desaturations are related to systemic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

early jugular bulb monitoring is useful in the emergency management of patients after severe traumatic brain damage, and that the first jugular bulb oximetery data should be interpreted in the context of all other systemic variables.

the initial jugular bulb oxygenation data obtained in the first hours following severe traumatic brain injury are very useful to identify the need for aggressive management of systemic factors that may impair cerebral perfusion.
jugular venous oxygenation (SjvO2) is an important parameter to be measured in the emergency management of patients with severe brain injury.
